hints: Start by turning each electronic configuration into a real element and its group, so you know who wants to lose or gain electrons.
Notice that W (2,4) and X (2,6) are both non-metals, while Y (2,8,2) and Z (2,8,8,1) are metals combining with non-metal X.
Recall which type of bonding gives small molecules that are gases at room temperature, and which gives giant lattices with very high boiling points.
walkthrough:
**Identify the four elements**

Great first move is to name them from their shells. This tells you metal or non-metal straight away.

$$W = 2,4 = \text{carbon, C (Group IV)}$$ $$X = 2,6 = \text{oxygen, O (Group VI)}$$ $$Y = 2,8,2 = \text{magnesium, Mg (Group II)}$$ $$Z = 2,8,8,1 = \text{potassium, K (Group I)}$$

**Work out the bonding in each compound**

Now look at who is combining with who. Non-metal with non-metal means covalent, metal with non-metal means ionic.

$$1. \text{WX}_2 = \text{CO}_2: \text{C + O, covalent molecular}$$ $$2. \text{YX} = \text{MgO: Mg + O, ionic}$$ $$3. \text{Z}_2\text{X} = \text{K}_2\text{O: K + O, ionic}$$

**Link structure to boiling point**

This is the key idea. Simple covalent molecules have weak intermolecular forces, so little energy is needed to separate them. They are gases or volatile liquids.

$$\text{CO}_2 \text{ is a simple molecule, a gas at room temperature, bp below } 25^{\circ}\text{C}$$

**Check the ionic compounds**

Ionic compounds form a giant lattice with strong electrostatic attraction in all directions. Lots of heat is needed to break this.

$$\text{MgO and K}_2\text{O are giant ionic solids with very high melting and boiling points}$$ 
So only 1 has a boiling point below room temperature.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all low boiling. While WX2 (CO2) is correct, YX (MgO) and Z2X (K2O) are giant ionic lattices with strong ionic bonds and boiling points far above room temperature.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 are both low boiling. WX2 (CO2) is a simple covalent gas, but YX (MgO) is ionic. Students choosing this forget that a Group II metal with a Group VI non-metal forms a high-melting ionic solid, not a molecule.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 are low boiling. Both YX (MgO) and Z2X (K2O) are formed from a metal plus oxygen, so both are ionic solids with giant structures and very high boiling points.
options.D: Correct. Only 1 is right. WX2 is CO2, a simple covalent molecule with weak van der Waals forces between molecules, so it is a gas with a boiling point below room temperature. YX and Z2X are ionic solids with high boiling points.
